global_rules.rule: No burned-in captions or subtitles, in any video, long or Short. Ship the .srt file instead.
global_rules.why: Owner rule, flagged repeatedly. The engine only draws captions if a spec sets burn_captions, and none may.

global_rules.rule: Every subcontinent name (first and last) and Indian place name is written in Devanagari in the narration.
global_rules.why: The voice (ElevenLabs Ruhaan) mispronounces Latin spellings. voice_lint.py fails the build otherwise.

global_rules.rule: Say "Under nineteen", write "T-twenty", and spell every number out. No digits in the narration.
global_rules.why: Digits and short forms are misread, especially next to Devanagari.

global_rules.rule: Hook in two seconds: the key number or claim is on screen before anything else.
global_rules.why: Retention drops fastest in the first seconds, especially on Shorts.

global_rules.rule: No broadcast footage, player photos, team or league logos, or likeness of a real person.
global_rules.why: Copyright and monetisation safety. Players are our illustrated avatars in team colours.

global_rules.rule: Every fact that can change is checked on the web; every headline number against an official source.
global_rules.why: Accuracy is the brand. Lessons: the Aaryavir debut figure, the Cricsheet gaps, one Rashid wicket.

global_rules.rule: Every spec carries sources[], including how the data was filtered.
global_rules.why: Goes into the description, and lets us defend any number.

global_rules.rule: Label illustrative visuals (field plans, replays) as illustrative.
global_rules.why: Honesty about what is drawn from data and what is a reconstruction.

global_rules.rule: Write for the ear: short sentences, a comma wherever a narrator would breathe.
global_rules.why: Pauses come from punctuation; long runs sound rushed.

global_rules.rule: Vary the venue, the camera and the poses from scene to scene; use synthesised sound effects.
global_rules.why: Keeps a faceless channel from looking the same every time.

formats.name: The Replay Room
formats.pitch: What really happened in the match, who decided it and why: from every ball's line, length, shot, control and direction.
formats.trigger: An India international finishes. Post the long video within 24 hours, Shorts the same day.
formats.data: Cricinfo + Cricbuzz match captures (tools/ttm-capture) for ODIs and Tests; Sportmonks for T20Is and the IPL. Cross-checked over by over and against the official scorecard.
formats.look: Lab charts for the numbers, Tactics Board for field plans, stadium-stage replays with the illustrated players for key shots.
beats: Cold open: the number that explains the match (0–2 s)
The turning point: control and run rate across all 50 overs, the phase where it was won
The innings that decided it: told ball by ball, with false shots and dropped catches marked
The hidden hero: the player the scorecard undersells (the luck meter: false shots drawn vs wickets)
The plan: where the field was, where the runs went
What if: the runs scored after each drop
Verdict and what it means for the next match
visuals: Wagon wheel that builds shot by shot
Pitch map of line and length
Innings timeline with false shots and drops
Illustrated replays: real shot direction and length
rules: Only our own graphics. Never copy Cricinfo or Cricbuzz charts, images or commentary text.
Cricbuzz notes are leads: verify each one against the ball data before it is said.
Credit "ball-by-ball data: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz" in the description sources.
Label replays "Illustrated from ball-tracking data".
Use "in control" / "not in control" for the shot-control field; don't invent new metrics without explaining them on screen.

formats.name: Myth or Data?
formats.pitch: Take something everyone says ("Kohli fails in knockouts") and settle it with the numbers, ending on a verdict stamp.
formats.length: Short 1–1.5 min; long 4–6 min when the evidence is rich
formats.trigger: A claim is trending: a commentator's line, a social-media debate, a milestone that revives an old argument. Post within 2–3 days.
formats.data: Sportmonks (IPL, T20Is), Cricsheet (Tests, ODIs; check completeness), official records.
formats.look: Theme "stadium": stage scenes with the illustrated player, poses per beat, the ball on shot moments, opponent avatar on versus beats.
beats: The claim, on screen in two seconds
The evidence, two or three numbers
Verdict stamp: busted / half true / confirmed
visuals: Stadium stage with venue matched to the real ground
Poses: walk, stance, drive, pull, celebrate, dejected
rules: Always end on the verdict stamp, so the series has a recognisable sign-off.
State the definition used (e.g. which matches count as knockouts).
Never present Cricsheet sums as career totals without checking the official record.

formats.name: The Lab
formats.pitch: A question only a model can answer: statistical twins, clusters, eras compared. Editorial-paper look, numbered episodes.
formats.trigger: Evergreen. Quiet weeks with no India cricket, end of a season, or when a player's season begs comparison.
formats.data: Sportmonks IPL 2013–2026 ball-by-ball (and captured internationals as they accumulate).
formats.look: Theme "lab": editorial paper, round tabs, lab_dots / lab_swarm / lab_radial / lab_rings / lab_units / lab_big. Title card with the player in a yellow disc and stat chips.
beats: Title card with the question and two stat chips
The checks (drop one measure, raise the bar, reverse search)
rules: Generate the spec from the analysis script and assert every claim in code.
Show the robustness checks on screen.
Count dismissals correctly (bowled rows carry no out_id).

formats.name: Stat Check
formats.pitch: "X or Y?" settled in rounds with a running scorecard and a final verdict.
formats.trigger: A debate between two players: trades, awards, selection, auction buzz, a rivalry in a live series.
formats.data: Sportmonks ball-by-ball; official records for career totals.
formats.look: Theme "lab" with the split-colour VS title card (both players in their kits, VS stamp), lab_vs and lab_score.
beats: Round 1…N: one measure each, league average for context
visuals: Split team-colour title with VS stamp
rules: Every round compares like with like (same phases, minimum balls).
Avoid any figure you can't reconcile with the official record (e.g. one Rashid wicket).

formats.name: Tactics Board
formats.pitch: How a match will be or was won: field plans, lengths, matchups, drawn on a tilted field.
formats.trigger: 1–3 days before a series or Test (preview), or after a match decided by a plan.
formats.data: Sportmonks for T20Is/IPL; captures and Cricsheet for ODIs/Tests; squad news from the web.
formats.look: "board" scenes (navy or cream), pucks, zones, ball paths, length band, mixed with Lab charts.
visuals: Tilted field with pucks and zones
rules: Label every field "Illustrative".
One label per zone (no stacked fielder labels).
Re-check squads and fitness the day before posting.

formats.name: What If?
formats.pitch: History rewritten with numbers: Bradman in the IPL, Sachin in the T20 era. Sepia film, back to colour at the end.
formats.trigger: Anniversaries, a legend in the news, or evergreen weekend slots.
formats.data: Career records, era-adjusted comparisons (z-scores), Sportmonks for the modern side.
formats.look: Stadium stage with "film": true (sepia), opening newspaper-style clipping (illustrative, no real masthead); last content scene in colour.
beats: The clipping: the moment history turned
Back to colour: what it would have meant
rules: Make the assumptions explicit on screen.
No real newspaper masthead or logo.

formats.name: Rising Star
formats.pitch: A trading card flips: the illustrated player on the front, verified numbers on the back.
formats.length: Short about 1 min (long when the story is big enough)
formats.trigger: A breakout performance by an Under nineteen, domestic or debut player; auction buzz. Within 48 hours.
formats.data: Official scorecards and reputable reports; youth data is thin, so verify each figure twice.
formats.look: Theme "card": flipping trading card, then stage scenes.
beats: The card flips: the headline number
rules: Triple-check "debut" and "record" claims (Aaryavir lesson).
Associate-team matches are not official Youth ODIs: no record claims from them.

formats.name: Flip
formats.pitch: No narration: one player against the best at the same point in their careers, card by card.
formats.trigger: A milestone, a player passing a legend, or a news hook (trade, captaincy).
formats.data: Cricsheet / Sportmonks; only players whose whole careers are in the data.
formats.look: flips.py: bold colour cards, one number each, flip transitions.
rules: State the cut-off ("after 52 Tests") on the first card.
Re-check totals after any new match.

formats.name: Milestone & News Shorts
formats.pitch: One number, one story, out before the moment: "22 runs from 2,000", a trade in one stat.
formats.length: Short 20–40 s (long only for big news like a trade)
formats.trigger: A milestone within reach before a match, a trade or announcement. Must post before the event; it expires.
formats.look: Blue "Men in Blue" theme, big number, kinetic text.
rules: Post before the match it refers to, or don't post it.
Mark the expiry in the tracker.

playbook.output: Long + 2–3 Shorts; IG carousel of the top 3 insights
playbook.prep: Capture Cricinfo + Cricbuzz after the match (both innings)

playbook.event: A series or Test starts in 1–3 days
playbook.output: Preview long + ground-guide Short / IG carousel

playbook.prep: Official record check; note the expiry

playbook.event: A claim or debate is trending
A quiet week, no India cricket
playbook.output: Lab episode or What If? long

cadence: About 3 long videos a week plus a daily Short. Long-form watch time comes first until monetisation: from 1 Feb 2027 new applicants need 8,000 watch hours (or 20M Shorts views in 90 days).
